label: the nasalisation marks: candrabindu, and the anusvara it is confused with
note: THIS POINT WAS HALF TRUE WHILE MARKED COVERED. Its label names the candrabindu AND the anusvaara it is confused with; the candrabindu had a lesson, the anusvaara had none, and HI-W12-chandrabindu said so in its own body -- 'there is a plain dot without the crescent ... FOR NOW: crescent plus dot means through the nose'. A lesson recording a debt it has no way to notice being paid, which is the fifth variety of stale claim catalogued in lessons.d. THE ANUSVAARA IS THE MOST-USED GLYPH THE CORPUS NEVER TAUGHT: 60 headwords, from chapter 2, including main, hain, mein and hindii. HI-S148-sign-anusvara draws it at chapter 16 and the candrabindu's deferral is rewritten to point back at it rather than forward at nothing.
